verdict: Sales rose 11% to $25.0B with growth in all three businesses and a record $340B order backlog, and profit rose 35% to $2.58B despite a $363M charge from a customer bankruptcy at Pratt & Whitney.

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$36M is $345M of pension income minus $381M of net interest expense. The -$125M equity line is the profit share belonging to noncontrolling partners, so net income is the amount attributable to RTX common shareowners.

takeaways.title: Growth in every business
takeaways.text: Sales reached $25.0B. Raytheon grew fastest at +14% on naval and air-defense work, while Collins and Pratt & Whitney each grew about +10%.

takeaways.title: Record backlog
takeaways.text: More than $81B of new orders in the quarter took the backlog to a record $340B, and RTX raised its full-year sales, EPS and cash-flow outlook.

takeaways.title: Bankruptcy charge at Pratt & Whitney
takeaways.text: Reported Pratt profit fell 19% because of a $363M charge tied to a customer bankruptcy. Without it, segment profit rose 29%, helped by about $160M of tariff cost recovery.

oneTimers: A $363M charge at Pratt & Whitney related to a customer bankruptcy is included in reported operating profit.
Adjusted results include roughly $0.5B of IEEPA tariff cost recovery across the segments (about $250M at Collins and $160M at Pratt & Whitney), worth $0.25 of adjusted EPS.
GAAP profit also includes $448M of acquisition-accounting adjustments and a $159M gain on investments recorded in eliminations and other.
footerNote: RTX counts $161M of 'Other income, net' inside operating profit; it is shown as a negative cost line so the flow balances. The three segments sum to $25,644M before $679M of intersegment eliminations, shown as a fourth segment line so segments sum exactly to total net sales.
